//credentials: JSON has no comments, so the notes live in keys the loader ignores.
A 'credentials' entry is an OAuth client identity the proxy authenticates
itself with; a server references one by name and the proxy acquires a
short-lived token per grant instead of reading a long-lived bearer off
disk. Grant, token endpoint and client identity belong to the credential;
'scope' and 'audience' belong to the server the token is presented to,
because one client legitimately serves many resources.
private_key_jwt signs a short-lived assertion with a key the authorization
server never sees, so nothing replayable is transmitted. It needs the
client_credentials reads its secret from the environment variable named by
'client_secret_env'. There is no 'client_secret' field: a config carrying
one is refused at load, because this file gets committed and shared.
Relative paths resolve against this file's parent directory.
A credential replaces the deprecated tokens file for that server. Naming
both for the same server is refused at load.
//policy_bundles: A 'policy_bundles' entry attaches a policy bundle (Rego, CEL or Cedar)
to one server's tools, by server name. 'path' is relative to this file;
'config' is the object the bundle's fetch plan reads its config facts
from; 'engine' forces one where a directory carries several artifacts;
'single_use' names the credential fields to spend per call. A plan with
a 'wallet' source cannot be attached here: that lookup is code, and the
proxy refuses to start rather than run with it missing.

config.requesterJwk: <the requester's public JWK, as a JSON string>
